description:
Elixir allows `in` with a literal list or range in a guard (`when x in [false, nil]`, `when x in 1..3`); Elixir's own Kernel uses it. fz rewrites `in` to a call to `Enum.member?` (source_sugar.rs:137), which a guard refuses: "compiler2 case/with guards must be dispatch-pure" (jobs/body.rs:786), and the same for entry guards.

Expected: in a guard, `x in [a, b]` with a literal list is `x === a or x === b`, and `x in first..last//step` with literal bounds is the integer range test, as Elixir expands them; outside guards `in` stays Enumerable membership. Checked against Elixir on interp, run and build. Not needed by the distiller.

comments.text:
Reproducer and mechanism (JSON, 2026-11-17, develop):

defmodule M do
  def hex?(c) when c in 48..57 or c in 65..70, do: true
  def hex?(_c), do: false
end
dbg({M.hex?(50), M.hex?(66), M.hex?(1)})

interp, run and build all print: error[lower/unsupported]: compiler2 entry guards for hex?/1 are not dispatch-pure and cannot be planned. The same in in a body works.

Mechanism: source_sugar.rs (38, 149-155) rewrites x in r to Enum.member?(r, x) and a..b to Range.new(a, b, 1) regardless of guard context; walk_guard_calls (jobs/dispatch.rs ~599) refuses the remote call as NotAGuardExpr (raised dispatch.rs:140/862). pattern-matching.md's guard-callee list omits in.

Suggested fix: in guard context with literal bounds, rewrite to comparisons. Note: Elixir expands x in a..b in a guard to is_integer(x) and x >= a and x <= b, so the is_integer test belongs in the rewrite.

Priority evidence: lib/json.fz's hex-digit test wanted it and used comparisons instead. Not blocking.

title: in with a literal list or range is allowed in a guard, as in Elixir
